**TL;DR:** Video platforms for organizing training content store, organize, and deliver video-based learning. Kaltura is best for enterprise search hubs and searchable training libraries, Docebo fits multi-audience LMS needs, and LearnWorlds is best for branded course academies.


## What is a video platform for organizing training content?


A training[video platform](https://corp.kaltura.com/blog/video-platforms/) is software that stores, organizes, and delivers video-based learning materials. It provides a central place where employees, customers, partners, or students can access training content on demand. Unlike a general-purpose video hosting service, a training platform includes features designed for learning, such as structured courses, user permissions, progress tracking, quizzes, and reporting.


Most platforms also include tools for managing large video libraries. Administrators can group videos into learning paths, organize content with categories and tags, control who can view specified materials, and update training without distributing new files. This makes it easier to keep content current and ensure learners always access the latest version.

## Who uses training video platforms?


### Corporate Learning & Development teams


Corporate learning and development teams use training video platforms to manage employee learning programs across departments and locations. Common use cases include:


- Onboarding
- Compliance training
- Technical instruction
- Leadership development
- Software training
- Professional skills development


These teams can organize videos into role-based courses or learning paths. A new employee, for example, may receive a sequence covering company policies, security practices, required tools, and job-specific procedures. More experienced employees may be assigned advanced content based on their responsibilities or career goals.


Progress tracking helps learning teams monitor participation and completion. Administrators can identify employees who have not started required training, review assessment results, and generate reports for managers or auditors. This is especially important for regulated training, where the organization may need evidence that employees completed specific material.


***Related content: Read our guide to choosing an***[enterprise video platform](https://corp.kaltura.com/blog/enterprise-video-platform/) ***.***


### Human resources departments


Human resources departments use training video platforms to support:


- Onboarding
- Policy communication
- Benefits education
- Workplace conduct training
- Employee development


Video helps HR deliver the same core information to each employee while reducing the need to repeat live sessions. During onboarding, HR can provide videos explaining company policies, payroll procedures, leave rules, benefits enrollment, workplace expectations, and internal systems. New hires can review the material at their own pace and return to specific sections when questions arise.


HR teams also use video for mandatory training. Examples include anti-harassment training, data privacy instruction, workplace safety, code-of-conduct education, and security awareness. Completion tracking provides a record of who finished each course and when.


### Customer education teams


Customer education teams use training video platforms to help customers understand, adopt, and use a product. Training may include:


- Product onboarding
- Feature walkthroughs
- Configuration guides
- Troubleshooting instructions
- Best practices
- Certification programs


A structured video library gives customers a self-service resource they can access at any time. Instead of contacting support for common questions, users can search for a specific task and watch the relevant lesson. This can reduce repetitive support requests and shorten the time needed to solve basic problems.


Customer education teams often organize content by product, use case, user role, or experience level. A new customer may begin with setup and account configuration, while an advanced user may need videos on integrations, automation, or administration.


### Sales enablement teams


Sales enablement teams use training video platforms to prepare sales representatives for customer conversations. Content may cover:


- Products
- Pricing
- Value propositions
- Competitive positioning
- Objection handling
- Discovery methods
- Sales processes
- Industry knowledge


Video allows enablement teams to distribute updates quickly. When a product changes or a new competitor enters the market, the team can publish a short training module and assign it to the relevant sales groups. This is more controlled than sharing files through email or chat.


Sales teams can organize content by product line, market segment, region, or role. Account executives may receive training on discovery and negotiation, while sales engineers may need deeper technical demonstrations. New hires can follow a structured onboarding path before working with prospects.


### Schools, universities, and training providers


Schools, universities, and training providers use video platforms to deliver:


- Lectures
- Demonstrations
- Tutorials
- Recorded classes
- Self-paced courses


These platforms support online, blended, and classroom-based learning. Instructors can organize videos into courses, modules, or weekly lessons. Supporting materials such as slides, readings, assignments, and quizzes may be attached to each video. This creates a clear sequence for students and reduces confusion about what to study next.


On-demand video allows students to pause, replay, or review difficult material. This is useful for technical subjects, laboratory demonstrations, language learning, and step-by-step procedures. Captions and transcripts also improve accessibility and make content easier to search.


## Key features of video platforms for training content


### 1. Centralized video content library


A centralized video content library gives administrators one place to store, manage, and publish training videos. It replaces scattered files in shared drives, email threads, and separate hosting accounts. Learners can access approved content from a consistent interface instead of searching across multiple systems.


Administrators can control permissions, update videos, archive outdated material, and apply retention rules from the same platform. Central management also helps prevent duplicate content and ensures users see the latest version of each lesson.


***Related content: Read our article about***[video content management systems](https://corp.kaltura.com/blog/video-content-management-systems/) ***.***


### 2. Channels, categories, and playlists


Channels and categories group training videos by department, topic, audience, or skill level. For example, an organization may create separate channels for onboarding, compliance, product training, and leadership development. This structure makes large libraries easier to navigate.


Playlists arrange videos in a defined sequence. They can guide learners through a course, onboarding program, or certification path without requiring them to choose each lesson manually. Administrators can update the sequence as training requirements change.


### 3. Advanced search and metadata


Advanced search helps learners find training content without browsing through folders or long course lists. Platforms may search video titles, descriptions, tags, speaker names, transcripts, and custom fields. Filters can narrow results by topic, department, date, duration, or content type.


Metadata improves how videos are classified and retrieved. Administrators can add keywords, ownership details, version numbers, access levels, and expiration dates. Consistent metadata also supports reporting, automated recommendations, and content governance.


### 4. Automatic transcription and captions


Automatic transcription converts spoken audio into searchable text. Learners can use transcripts to review key points, locate a specific term, or follow the lesson without replaying the full video. Transcripts also make it easier for administrators to index and manage large video libraries.


Captions display spoken content on screen and improve accessibility for people who are deaf or hard of hearing. They are also useful in noisy environments or when learners cannot use audio. Platforms should allow editors to correct transcription errors, especially for technical terms and names.


### 5. Video quizzes and knowledge checks


Video quizzes place questions before, during, or after a training video. Common formats include multiple-choice questions, true-or-false items, short answers, and scenario-based checks. These questions help confirm that learners understand the material instead of only playing the video.


Knowledge checks can also reinforce important concepts and identify areas that require review. Platforms may require a passing score, allow repeated attempts, or direct learners back to a specific section after an incorrect answer. Results can be included in completion reports.


### 6. Progress and completion tracking


Progress tracking shows how much of a video or course each learner has completed. Administrators can see whether users started, paused, skipped, or finished assigned content. This is useful for onboarding, compliance, certification, and other programs with required training.


Completion rules can be based on watch percentage, quiz scores, lesson order, or assignment deadlines. Reports help managers identify overdue training and confirm that required learning has been completed. Some platforms can also send reminders or export records to a learning management system.


### 7. Live training and webinar support


Live training support allows instructors to deliver scheduled sessions through the same platform used for recorded content. Features may include screen sharing, chat, polls, question-and-answer tools, attendance tracking, and session moderation. This supports workshops, product demonstrations, and instructor-led classes.


Recorded live sessions can be added to the video library after the event. Administrators can edit the recording, add captions, attach resources, and assign it to users who could not attend. This creates a reusable training asset from a single live session.


### 8. AI-powered search and content recommendations


AI-powered search can interpret natural-language questions and return relevant videos, chapters, or transcript sections. Instead of matching only exact keywords, it can identify related concepts and direct learners to the point in a video where the topic is discussed.


Content recommendations suggest training based on a learner’s role, viewing history, assigned courses, or skill needs. These recommendations can help users discover relevant material in large libraries. Administrators should still review recommendation settings to prevent outdated or restricted content from appearing.


### 9. Agentic Avatars


Agentic Avatars use AI to understand a learner’s goals and questions, then organize training content around that real-time intent. Rather than presenting a fixed learning path, the avatar searches across videos, transcripts, documents, and other approved knowledge sources to identify the most relevant information. It can answer natural-language questions, explain concepts, or recommend the next training resource.


For administrators, Agentic Avatars make existing training libraries easier to use without requiring content to be manually reorganized for every audience or use case. The avatar adapts recommendations based on factors such as the learner’s role, permissions, previous training, and current task while respecting access controls.


## Notable video platforms for organizing training content


**How we selected these platforms:** We shortlisted video platforms for organizing training content based on their ability to store, organize, search, secure, and deliver video-based learning, along with features like progress tracking, quizzing, captioning, and LMS integration.


### Enterprise video platforms


#### 1. Kaltura Video Portal


**Best for:** A branded, secure video hub for a large organization
**Strengths:** Central content management, AI-powered content discovery and personalization, search, access control, analytics
**Things to consider:** Setup and full configuration benefit from technical support


Kaltura Video Portal is an enterprise video hub where an organization stores, organizes, and delivers on-demand video content. Teams establish, design, and manage a content hub that they can brand and control, with built-in tools for recording, editing, and enriching video.


Content management features make it easier to find, manage, and distribute videos across the organization, while access controls and a zero-trust approach support strict security requirements. AI capabilities add search across spoken words and on-screen text, generate clips, quizzes, summaries, and metadata from existing content, and power **Agentic Avatars** that dynamically organize and surface the most relevant content based on each user’s role, goals, context, and natural-language questions.


**Key features include:**


- **Content hub and management:** Administrators build a branded hub to organize, manage, and distribute content across the organization, with advanced search and filtering for content discovery.
- **Creation and enrichment tools:** Built-in self-recording, screen recording, and editing tools work alongside captions, quizzes, chapters, and dubbing to enrich videos.
- **AI search and repurposing:** Optical character recognition and automatic speech recognition make spoken words and on-screen text findable, while one-click tools generate clips, quizzes, summaries, and metadata from existing content.
- **Access control and security:** Access controls and a zero-trust approach support high security standards, with permissions managed across the hub.
- **Analytics dashboards:** Dashboards track engagement inside and outside the hub, down to granular data units and real-time traffic.
- **Branding and embeddable content:** Branding and modularity options control the look and feel of the portal, and an embeddable player distributes content beyond the hub.
- **Agentic content experiences:** AI-powered Agentic Avatars organize content in real time around each learner’s needs, delivering personalized guidance, and answering questions without requiring users to browse the content library.


**Limitations (as reported by users on G2):**


- **Learning curve at setup:** New users may need time to get comfortable, and initial configuration goes more smoothly when the internal technical team is involved.
- **Basic built-in editing:** The in-platform editing tools cover essentials such as trimming and clipping rather than advanced production.
- **Best value at scale:** The platform delivers the most value for organizations with large or growing video libraries.


Source:[Kaltura](https://corp.kaltura.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Message-Page@2x.png)


#### 2. Panopto


**Best for:** Governed, searchable training libraries inside the LMS


**Strengths:** Smart search, LMS integration, in-video quizzing, analytics


**Things to consider:** Some enhanced capabilities are paid add-ons


Panopto is a video platform for recording, managing, searching, and sharing training video at scale. L&D teams build a governed library where content is recorded once and delivered consistently across teams, roles, and locations, rather than scattered across shared drives.


Subject-matter experts record walkthroughs and demonstrations, or use the AI Video Studio add-on to turn scripts and slides into avatar-led video. Content is organized in a central, searchable library and reusable across programs and formats without re-recording.


**Key features include:**


- **Intelligent search:** Automatic speech recognition and optical character recognition index every spoken word, slide, and on-screen element, returning timestamped results across the library.
- **Governed video library:** Content lives in a centrally managed library with version control and folder-level retention policies, so only current, approved versions stay accessible.
- **LMS and workflow integration:** LTI-compliant integration with LMS and HR systems delivers training inside existing tools, and completion data flows back automatically.
- **In-video quizzes and knowledge checks:** Quizzes, branching scenarios, and knowledge checks embedded in videos give evidence of understanding alongside completion data.
- **Recording and content creation:** Recording works across computers, webcams, and AV equipment with non-destructive editing, and the AI Video Studio add-on generates avatar-led video from scripts or slides.
- **Analytics and translation:** Per-viewer data shows how much of each video employees watched, and one-click translation with automatic language detection supports global workforces.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/panopto/reviews) **):**


- **Enhanced features cost extra:** Several capabilities, including AI video generation and the video portal, are add-ons to an existing license.
- **Processing and interface speed:** Uploading or processing videos can take time, and browsing large folder hierarchies can feel slow.
- **Editing depth:** Editing handles trimming and cuts but lacks options such as separating audio from video or adding text overlays.
- **Folder-level permissions:** Editing permissions are managed at the folder level, so granting edit access can extend to other videos in the same folder.
- **Admin setup and reporting:** Some administrators report SSO setup and migration as involved, and admin-side reporting could be deeper.


Source:[Panopto](https://support.panopto.com/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka65Y0000008a9N&feoid=00N5Y00000UHUJw&refid=0EM5Y000006VQWu)


#### 3. EchoVideo (Echo360)


**Best for:** Managing and delivering video for education and corporate training


**Strengths:** Video CMS, lecture capture, LMS sync, in-video quizzing


**Things to consider:** Interface and search can feel dated to some users


EchoVideo is Echo360’s platform for creating, capturing, managing, storing, and searching video across education and corporate settings. It offers flexible cloud storage that ingests a video library into a single source, with organizational tools that let teams store content in courses for institutional learners or folders for corporate and deskless workers.


The platform supports both live and on-demand content and integrates with major LMS options through the LTI protocol, keeping video, rosters, calendars, and gradebooks in sync.


**Key features include:**


- **Video content management:** Cloud storage and organization tools store, manage, and search a video library, with folders for corporate learners and courses for institutional ones.
- **Lecture and screen capture:** One-click or scheduled recording captures lectures and training, with hardware and software capture options.
- **LMS integration and gradebook sync:** LTI integration keeps content in sync with the LMS, and automatic gradebook sync grades video assignments and returns results.
- **In-video quizzing:** Quizzes embedded directly in videos turn passive viewing into interactive learning.
- **Editing and splicing:** Browser-based editing lets users trim and splice new content into existing videos, with updates published automatically.
- **Captioning and analytics:** Automatic speech recognition transcribes videos into editable captions, and dashboards give administrators and instructors insight into engagement and system performance.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/echo360/reviews) **):**


- **Interface and organization:** Some users find the ways to organize and share videos confusing and the video player dated.
- **Missing conveniences:** Certain basic functions, such as editing playlists, are reported as absent.
- **Mobile apps:** Users report that the mobile apps need improvement.
- **Search performance:** Some administrators note slow or inaccurate search results.
- **Admin controls:** Reviewers cite limited permission customization for user roles and no simple dashboard to monitor contract usage.


Source:[Echo360](https://support.echo360.com/hc/article_attachments/11077408624397)


#### 4. YuJa Lumina Video Platform


**Best for:** Storing, managing, and streaming a compliant video library


**Strengths:** Cloud video CMS, search, captioning, quizzing, analytics


**Things to consider:** Product and integrations are education-first


YuJa Lumina is a cloud-based video platform for creating, managing, and distributing video content. Teams upload, organize, and manage a media library in the cloud, with search and categorization tools to control libraries of any size.


It supports on-demand and live video through a configurable, branded HTML5 player with interactive features, and it is LTI-compliant for embedding and streaming video inside an LMS. AI and machine learning generate metadata to improve search across the library.


**Key features include:**


- **Cloud video management:** Upload, organize, and manage a media library securely in the cloud, with search and categorization tools for libraries of any size.
- **Global streaming and player:** Adaptive bitrate streaming delivers video across devices through a branded HTML5 player that supports multiple streams and interactive features.
- **Video quizzing:** Interactive video quizzes measure retention and sync scores to the LMS gradebook.
- **Captioning and accessibility:** Automatic captioning, inline caption editing, and a Video Compliance Report track captions, audio descriptions, and chapters.
- **Advanced search and analytics:** AI-generated metadata supports search across the library, and engagement analytics track how viewers interact with content.
- **Capture and commenting:** Software, hardware, browser, and mobile capture tools record content, and time-stamped inline comments support contextual feedback.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/yuja/reviews) **):**


- **Education-first orientation:** The platform and its integrations are built primarily around higher-ed and K-12 workflows, so corporate teams should confirm fit.
- **Support consistency:** Some users report unresolved support tickets or slow resolution in certain cases.
- **Module breadth:** The platform spans many separate modules and add-ons, which can add setup and navigation complexity. Overall, user reviews for the platform skew positive.


Source:[YuJa](https://www.yuja.com/wp-content/uploads/Distribute-Content-2-1-scaled-1.png)


### Video Learning and Course Platforms


#### 5. Docebo


**Best for:** Multi-audience training and compliance from one platform


**Strengths:** AI content tools, automation, analytics, LMS and LXP in one


**Things to consider:** Advanced capabilities and setup can require time


Docebo is an AI-powered learning platform that lets organizations create, deliver, and manage training for employees, customers, and partners from a single system. It combines elements of an LMS, LXP, authoring tool, content management, virtual classroom, and analytics.


The platform manages multiple audiences and use cases in a centralized, organized way, including onboarding, compliance, sales enablement, and customer education, with AI tools built in for content creation, search, and administration.


**Key features include:**


- **Multi-audience learning management:** One platform delivers training to employees, customers, and partners, with learner groups, roles, and localization for global audiences.
- **AI content creation:** Docebo Creator and AI workflows generate interactive content and full learning plans, alongside a marketplace of over 30,000 courses.
- **Automation:** Automates enrollments, translations, and content categorization to reduce manual admin work.
- **Compliance and certification:** Enrollment rules, certification programs with validity periods, and automated renewals support compliance tracking.
- **Analytics and reporting:** Dashboards and custom reports measure adoption, progress, and impact, with BI integration.
- **Integrations and standards:** Native integrations connect HRIS, CRM, e-commerce, and SSO, a headless option embeds learning in other tools, and the platform supports SCORM, xAPI, and AICC.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/docebo/reviews) **):**


- **Reporting customization:** Deeper or custom reports can feel limited, and some users export data to spreadsheets for detailed audits.
- **Learning curve:** The platform is feature-dense, and setting up custom reports, workflows, or integrations can require time and, at times, developer help.
- **Customization limits:** Some users cite limits on branding, layouts, and certificate templates.
- **Add-ons and pricing:** Several advanced capabilities are paid add-ons, and pricing is quote-based.
- **Support and mobile:** Some users report slow support responses and a mobile experience that is less smooth than desktop.


Source:[Docebo](https://help.docebo.com/hc/article_attachments/17395338200338)


#### 6. Vimeo


**Best for:** Hosting and delivering training video with LMS analytics


**Strengths:** Secure video library, LMS embedding, interactive video


**Things to consider:** Video-hosting-first, with lighter course structure


Vimeo’s learning and development solution centers on a secure, centralized video library for training content. Videos are automatically transcribed so they are searchable by any spoken word or phrase, and teams embed Vimeo-hosted videos into an LMS.


Using SCORM or xAPI, teams deliver video and pass user-level analytics back to the LMS. Interactive video adds in-video quizzes and clickable branches, and role-based permissions control which departments see which content.


**Key features include:**


- **Centralized video library:** A secure video library consolidates training content, with automatic transcription that makes videos searchable by spoken word.
- **LMS integration:** SCORM and xAPI embedding delivers Vimeo-hosted video into an LMS, with user-level analytics passed back.
- **Interactive video:** In-video quizzes, clickable hot spots, and branching let viewers choose their path and pause for questions.
- **Recording and editing:** Browser recording, an AI-assisted teleprompter, and text-based editing support content creation, including removing filler words.
- **Analytics and access controls:** Team analytics and engagement graphs show which videos employees watched and where they dropped off, and role-based permissions tailor folder access.
- **Mobile and AI:** Mobile apps allow browsing and recording, and AI generates summaries, highlight reels, and translations.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/vimeo/reviews) **):**


- **Cost and tiers:** Useful features sit behind higher tiers, and pricing can be a hurdle for smaller teams.
- **Storage and bandwidth caps:** Paid plans carry storage and monthly bandwidth limits that some teams reach faster than expected.
- **Large-library management:** Managing very large libraries can be cumbersome, with limited items per page and slower loading of long lists.
- **Enterprise-only security:** Features such as DRM, watermarking, and SSO are limited to the Enterprise plan.
- **Support responsiveness:** Some users report slower support for non-enterprise plans.


Source:[Vimeo](https://help.vimeo.com/hc/article_attachments/41073116599953)


#### 7. LearnWorlds


**Best for:** Building branded course academies with interactive video


**Strengths:** Interactive video, assessments, SCORM, white-label academy


**Things to consider:** Some features and page limits are tier-gated


LearnWorlds is a course and learning platform for creating, delivering, and selling training through branded online academies. It turns content into courses and structured programs with interactive activities, flexible assessments, and interactive video.


Teams build a white-label website and mobile app, manage learners with custom roles and analytics, and sell training through built-in checkout, bundles, and subscriptions. It also supports SCORM/HTML5 packages and LTI for bringing external tools into one training experience.


**Key features include:**


- **Course and program builder:** Build courses and structured programs as learning paths or curated collections, with sequential navigation and prerequisites.
- **Interactive video:** The interactive video editor adds questions, buttons, pop-ups, branching, and auto-generated transcripts, with analytics on plays and drop-offs.
- **Assessments and certificates:** An assessment builder creates exams and self-assessments, with certificates issued on completion.
- **SCORM and LTI:** Upload SCORM/HTML5 packages and bring external learning tools into one experience through LTI.
- **White-label academy:** A no-code website and mobile app builder produces a fully branded, white-label academy.
- **Analytics, roles, and commerce:** Reporting gives insight on learning impact, custom user roles set access levels, and built-in cart, bundles, and subscriptions support selling training.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/learnworlds/reviews) **):**


- **Tier-gated features:** Interactive video and app publishing sit on higher plans, and the entry plan limits the number of pages.
- **Enrollment fees:** The Starter plan adds a per-enrollment charge that can accumulate.
- **Admin role flexibility:** Some users want more granular, course-locked administrator roles.
- **Learning curve:** The platform is feature-dense, and some menu labels and options can feel confusing at first.
- **Mobile and uploads:** Some users report a limited mobile experience and a limit on the number of videos uploaded at once.


Source:[LearnWorlds](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12161576750/original/BqFE5AISN6SjZVFpvLluxDeGV6aYWPdWkQ.png?1747734293)


#### 8. Uscreen


**Best for:** Training providers monetizing an on-demand video library


**Strengths:** Netflix-style library, apps, live streaming, community


**Things to consider:** Built for video memberships, with light LMS features


Uscreen is a video membership platform for turning a video library into a subscription business, used by educators, coaches, and media businesses. Teams upload, organize, and stream content in a Netflix-style catalog on their own branded website, mobile apps, and TV apps.


It combines on-demand video, live streaming, and community features in one place, with flexible monetization such as subscriptions, free trials, and one-off courses.


**Key features include:**


- **Video library and catalog:** Upload and organize content into a Netflix-style catalog where members can comment, download, and build playlists.
- **Branded apps:** Mobile and TV apps launch without coding, with push notifications to keep members engaged.
- **Live streaming:** Native live streaming lets members join from any device and chat live, with a calendar tool that sends reminders.
- **Community:** Built-in public and private channels let members connect alongside the video library.
- **Monetization:** Subscriptions, free trials, one-off courses, and varied payment options support recurring revenue.
- **Marketing and analytics:** Built-in marketing tools and analytics track payments, engagement, and video performance.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/147245/Uscreen/) **):**


- **Light learning management:** The platform is built for video memberships rather than formal courses, so learning-management features are limited.
- **Content type focus:** It centers on video content, with limited support for other content formats.
- **Membership flexibility:** Options for membership levels and trials are somewhat limited, and the community feature is relatively basic.
- **Library management:** Some users note limits around thumbnails, playlists, looping, and bulk uploads.
- **Support and pricing:** Some users report inconsistent support follow-through, and pricing can be higher than entry-level tools.


Source:[Uscreen](https://cdn.uscreen.tv/uscreen/65988bbc531ac2845a272d33_your-salt-water-guide-community.png?auto=format,compress&w=1117&h=708)


## Conclusion


A video platform for organizing training content helps organizations manage the full lifecycle of video-based learning, from content creation and organization to delivery, tracking, and ongoing maintenance. The right platform depends on factors such as audience size, governance requirements, learning management integration, collaboration features, and reporting needs. Organizations should prioritize platforms that make content easy to discover, keep training materials up to date, support measurable learning outcomes, and scale as their training library and user base grow.
